MA.5.AR.1.1.statement_verified: Solve multi-step real-world problems involving any combination of the four operations with whole numbers, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted within the context.

MA.5.AR.1.AP.1.statement_verified: Solve one- and two-step real-world problems involving any combination of the four operations with whole numbers. Explore problems in which remainders must be interpreted within the context.

MA.5.AR.1.2.statement_verified: Solve real-world problems involving the addition, subtraction or multiplication of fractions, including mixed numbers and fractions greater than 1.

MA.5.AR.1.AP.2a.statement_verified: Solve one-step real-world problems involving addition and subtraction of mixed numbers and fractions greater than one with like denominators.

MA.5.AR.1.AP.2b.statement_verified: Solve one-step real-world problems involving multiplication of unit fractions.

MA.5.AR.1.3.statement_verified: Solve real-world problems involving division of a unit fraction by a whole number and a whole number by a unit fraction.

MA.5.AR.1.AP.3.statement_verified: Solve one-step real-world problems involving division of a whole number by a unit fraction.

MA.5.AR.2.1.statement_verified: Translate written real-world and mathematical descriptions into numerical expressions and numerical expressions into written mathematical descriptions.

MA.5.AR.2.AP.1.statement_verified: Translate mathematical descriptions (e.g., five plus two; the product of three and four) into numerical expressions with two terms.

MA.5.AR.2.2.statement_verified: Evaluate multi-step numerical expressions using order of operations.

MA.5.AR.2.AP.2.statement_verified: Evaluate an expression containing three terms and one set of parentheses.

MA.5.AR.2.3.statement_verified: Determine and explain whether an equation involving any of the four operations is true or false.

MA.5.AR.2.AP.3.statement_verified: Determine whether an equation (with no more than four terms and up to one set of parentheses) involving any of the four operations with whole numbers is true or false. Limit addition and subtraction to within 100 and limit multiplication and division to the products of two single-digit whole numbers and their related division facts.

MA.5.AR.2.4.statement_verified: Given a mathematical or real-world context, write an equation involving any of the four operations to determine the unknown whole number with the unknown in any position.

MA.5.AR.2.AP.4.statement_verified: Given a mathematical or real-world context, generate an equation involving any of the four operations to determine the unknown sum, difference, product or quotient. Sums may not exceed 100 and their related subtraction facts. Multiplication and division may not exceed two digit by one digit.

MA.5.AR.3.1.statement_verified: Given a numerical pattern, identify and write a rule that can describe the pattern as an expression.

MA.5.AR.3.AP.1.statement_verified: Given a numerical pattern, identify a one-step rule that can describe the pattern.

MA.5.AR.3.2.statement_verified: Given a rule for a numerical pattern, use a two-column table to record the inputs and outputs.

MA.5.AR.3.AP.2.statement_verified: Given the inputs and a one-step addition or subtraction rule for a numerical pattern, use a two-column table to record the outputs.

MA.5.M.1.1.statement_verified: Solve multi-step real-world problems that involve converting measurement units to equivalent measurements within a single system of measurement.

MA.5.M.1.AP.1a.statement_verified: Using a conversion sheet, convert within a single system of measurement using the units: miles, yards, feet, inches; pounds, ounces; gallons, quarts, pints, cups; and hours, minutes. Only whole number measurements may be used.

MA.5.M.1.AP.1b.statement_verified: Using a conversion sheet, solve one-and two-step real-world problems that involve converting measurement units (i.e., miles, yards, feet, inches; pounds, ounces; gallons, quarts, pints, cups; and hours, minutes) to equivalent measurements within a single system of measurement. Only whole number measurements may be used.

MA.5.M.2.1.statement_verified: Solve multi-step real-world problems involving money using decimal notation.

MA.5.M.2.AP.1.statement_verified: Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction real-world problems involving money using decimal notation with all terms less than $20.00 (e.g., $11.74 + $5.31, $10.99 − $3.26).

MA.5.FR.1.1.statement_verified: Given a mathematical or real-world problem, represent the division of two whole numbers as a fraction.

MA.5.FR.1.AP.1.statement_verified: Explore the connection between fractions and division in a real-world problem.

MA.5.FR.2.1.statement_verified: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators, including mixed numbers and fractions greater than 1, with procedural reliability.

MA.5.FR.2.AP.1a.statement_verified: Explore adding and subtracting mixed numbers and fractions greater than 1 with like denominators.

MA.5.FR.2.AP.1b.statement_verified: Explore adding and subtracting fractions less than one with unlike denominators. where one denominator is a multiple of the other (e.g., + , − ).

MA.5.FR.2.2.statement_verified: Extend previous understanding of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a fraction, including mixed numbers and fractions greater than 1, with procedural reliability.

MA.5.FR.2.AP.2.statement_verified: Explore multiplying a unit fraction by a unit fraction.

MA.5.FR.2.3.statement_verified: When multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 or a fraction greater than 1, predict and explain the relative size of the product to the given number without calculating.

MA.5.FR.2.AP.3.statement_verified: Explore the impact on the size of the product when multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 or by a whole number.

MA.5.FR.2.4.statement_verified: Extend previous understanding of division to explore the division of a unit fraction by a whole number and a whole number by a unit fraction.

MA.5.FR.2.AP.4.statement_verified: Explore the division of a one-digit whole number by a unit fraction. Denominators are limited to 2, 3 or 4.

MA.5.GR.1.1.statement_verified: Classify triangles or quadrilaterals into different categories based on shared defining attributes. Explain why a triangle or quadrilateral would or would not belong to a category.

MA.5.GR.1.AP.1a.statement_verified: Sort triangles into different categories based on the size of their angles. Triangles include acute, obtuse and right.

MA.5.GR.1.AP.1b.statement_verified: Sort quadrilaterals into different categories based on shared defining attributes. Explore why a quadrilateral would or would not belong to a category. Quadrilaterals include parallelograms, rhombi, rectangles, squares and trapezoids.

MA.5.GR.1.2.statement_verified: Identify and classify three-dimensional figures into categories based on their defining attributes. Figures are limited to right pyramids, right prisms, right circular cylinders, right circular cones and spheres.

MA.5.GR.1.AP.2.statement_verified: Identify and sort three-dimensional figures into categories based on their defining attributes. Figures are limited to right rectangular pyramids, right rectangular prisms, right circular cylinders, right circular cones and spheres.

MA.5.GR.2.1.statement_verified: Find the perimeter and area of a rectangle with fractional or decimal side lengths using visual models and formulas.

MA.5.GR.2.AP.1.statement_verified: Find the perimeter and area of a rectangle with decimal side lengths using a visual model and calculator.

MA.5.GR.3.1.statement_verified: Explore volume as an attribute of three-dimensional figures by packing them with unit cubes without gaps. Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by counting unit cubes.

MA.5.GR.3.AP.1.statement_verified: Explore volume as an attribute of three-dimensional figures that can be measured by packing them with unit cubes without gaps.

MA.5.GR.3.2.statement_verified: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths using a visual model and a formula.

MA.5.GR.3.AP.2.statement_verified: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by counting unit cubes. Explore that the volume is the same as what would be found by multiplying the edge lengths.

MA.5.GR.3.3.statement_verified: Solve real-world problems involving the volume of right rectangular prisms, including problems with an unknown edge length, with whole-number edge lengths using a visual model or a formula. Write an equation with a variable for the unknown to represent the problem.

MA.5.GR.3.AP.3.statement_verified: Solve real-world problems involving the volume of right rectangular prisms with given whole-number edge lengths using a visual model or formula.

MA.5.GR.4.1.statement_verified: Identify the origin and axes in the coordinate system. Plot and label ordered pairs in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.

MA.5.GR.4.AP.1.statement_verified: Explore the first quadrant of the coordinate plane including the origin, axes and points located by using ordered pairs.

MA.5.GR.4.2.statement_verified: Represent mathematical and real-world problems by plotting points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

MA.5.GR.4.AP.2.statement_verified: Plot and label ordered pairs in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.

MA.5.DP.1.1.statement_verified: Collect and represent numerical data, including fractional and decimal values, using tables, line graphs or line plots.

MA.5.DP.1.AP.1.statement_verified: Sort and represent numerical data, including fractional values using tables or line plots (when given a scaled number line). Data set to include only whole numbers, halves and quarters.

MA.5.DP.1.2.statement_verified: Interpret numerical data, with whole-number values, represented with tables or line plots by determining the mean, mode, median or range.

MA.5.DP.1.AP.2.statement_verified: Interpret numerical data, with whole-number values, represented with tables or line plots by determining the mean, mode or range. Line plot scales to include only whole numbers, halves and quarters.

MA.2.AR.3.AP.2.statement_verified: Explore using repeated addition to find the total number of objects represented in a collection of equal groups (e.g., 3 groups of 2 objects) or in a rectangular array (e.g., 3 rows of 2 objects). Total objects may not exceed 20.

MA.2.M.1.2.statement_verified: Measure the lengths of two objects using the same unit and determine the difference between their measurements.

MA.2.M.2.1.statement_verified: Using analog and digital clocks, tell and write time to the nearest five minutes using a.m. and p.m. appropriately. Express portions of an hour using the fractional terms half an hour, half past, quarter of an hour, quarter after and quarter til.

MA.2.M.2.2.statement_verified: Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction real-world problems involving either dollar bills within $100 or coins within 100¢ using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.

MA.2.GR.1.3.statement_verified: Identify line(s) of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure.

MA.2.GR.1.AP.3.statement_verified: Identify a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure.

MA.K12.MTR.1.1.statement_verified: Actively participate in effortful learning both individually and collectively.Mathematicians who participate in effortful learning both individually and with others: Analyze the problem in a way that makes sense given the task.Ask questions that will help with solving the task.Build perseverance by modifying methods as needed while solving a challenging task.Stay engaged and maintain a positive mindset when working to solve tasks.Help and support each other when attempting a new method or approach.
